Straightforward suggestion, if the user's upkarmas is greater than the limit set by the site (x), it will simply show ">x"

eg. if x = 1,000 and username has 1,040 upsubmissions and 673 upposts, this is what their username bar will show

Username >1,000 | 673
When users have more than x amount of upkarmas, it just displays ">x"

Like I said in https://voat.co/v/ideasforvoat/comments/63302/93208, I agree for some displayed limit for "Submission contribution points" and "Comment contribution point" values. I'm thinking this would help to curb any knee-jerk, thoughtless moderation based on a user's current score.

An idea of just displaying percentage values in place of those scores might be worth a discussion too.

But... but... I like seeing my real numbers! Seeing my score go up lets my know there is activity in one of my posts and I can revisit the page to see the new comments (that aren't directly to me).

I could see a GROSS > LIMIT type format, just so you can see the limit for that sub easily. But I would hate it not being able to see my current score easily.

One of the things Reddit did to obfuscate their astroturfing of certain posts was to remove the Scores from posts. This seems way way too similar, even if its on a personal level.

That's a good point about seeing your own score. I think I'd quite like to see if I have a million points. But I don't think other users should see that score when visiting a profile because of how that can affect how they rate a comment or post.

Let me ask you though - if you saw that you had a million points, do you think that would alter how you rate other comments or posts?

Not at all. But it does let you have a bit more freedom while posting your own opinions.

My Reddit account has >100,000 comment karma. The only real change having high karma brought was the luxury of not caring about Karma. I could say what I actually thought in a circlejerk and take -80 karma and not care. I used to call it my "Karma Cushion".

I could say what I actually thought in a circlejerk and take -80 karma and not care

That means knowing your own karma score influenced how you acted, no? I'm pretty sure everyone agrees these are imaginary internet points which have no meaning in real life (at least until some sort of monetary exchange program is put into place). Yet you felt inhibited when you didn't have enough karma, and uninhibited when you had karma to burn?

I don't think so. I think its a post justification. Like people will do what people will do regardless, but after the fact when the ship is sinking how upset they get with the repercussions is influenced.

Its like the other day on here I saw a guy being a major dick to another poster, he got downvoated to -2 or -3 per post. Then he deleted every single post he ever made (basically reset his account).

So did his score affect his actions? Not before hand, but yes after the fact. He was a dick ether way, but once his score dropped then he deleted the posts. Maybe if he had a huge score -2s and -3s wouldn't have affected him enough to make him want to delete, but thats still after the fact. He was a dick ether way.

Same deal with me. I'd probably post the same thing ether way, but having the karma cushion let me care a lot less how things played out AFTER I posted.
